function: system (p. 4, p. 5): over-the-air FL aggregation (AirComp with truncated channel inversion, compared with digital FDMA) between single-antenna devices and a single-antenna PS over scalar Rayleigh channels, no RIS; area 7.
notes: Reason system, in an area 7 work. p. 4: "Let hbar_k = d_k^(-alpha/2) h_k be the channel between the k-th device and the PS" and "Assume that the channels are independent Rayleigh fadings, i.e., h_k ~ CN(0, 1)"; the notation of p. 3 puts vectors in boldface, and these channels are scalars. p. 5: the received signal is "y = sum_k chi_k hbar_k beta_k g_m^k + z_m", where "beta_k is the pre-processing factor at device k" (scalar truncated channel inversion, eq. (15)) and there is no receive beamformer, so the devices and the PS each have one antenna; y is a vector only because it carries the d entries of the gradient. No RIS: RIS and multi-antenna receivers appear only in the related work (p. 1 ref. [22], p. 2 ref. [33]), and the simulation settings (p. 11) and figure legends (pp. 10-12, checked on the page images) vary only power, quantization bits, CSI accuracy rho, truncation threshold, number of devices, and the sampling scheme. Earlier checks: FL over the air passes no_learning; it is not a survey, since it adds a convergence analysis and a device sampling optimization with numerical results (p. 2); the analog scheme performs AirComp aggregation (p. 5), so it is not purely digital FL (function check); its device sampling acts on the aggregation, because the inclusion probabilities enter the pre-equalization in (15) and the equivalent noise in (44) (pp. 5, 9), so I did not treat it as scheduling above the physical layer. The only learned element is the FL model (MLP on MNIST, CNN on CIFAR-10, pp. 10-11); the sampling optimization is classical (KKT and Dinkelbach, pp. 9-10). The PDF is arXiv:2405.17759v1 and matches the DOI (same title and authors in the DOI metadata).
